sections.title: Fats
sections.narration: 30.7 grams of fat. Omega 3 is huge at 17.83 grams, which is the main reason chia stands out. Saturated fat is 3.3 grams, so it stays fairly controlled for such a fatty seed. Polyunsaturated fat is 23.7 grams, another strong fat-quality mark. For seeds, fat quality is a big part of the ranking.

sections.title: Pros
sections.narration: Pros first: fuller texture helps real meals. The gel can make yogurt, oats, and smoothies feel more filling. ALA omega-3 is the headline fat. That is the food-specific reason chia stands out among seeds. Easy to boost meals invisibly. A small spoonful can disappear into everyday meals.

sections.title: Cons
sections.narration: Cons next: works best with enough fluid. Dry chia is awkward unless it is soaked or mixed properly. Phytates add an absorption caveat. The mineral numbers are high, but absorption is not automatic. Gel texture and digestion can be divisive. The same thing that helps satiety can put some people off.
